chapter: Sam Morgan, repertoire and Silver Leaf
title: Chris Kelly and filling his jobs
summary: He played jobs for Chris Kelly when Kelly was double-booked; Kelly did not read.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: And that reminds me, did you ever hear Chris Kelly?

Oh yeah, yeah, I know Chris Kelly, I know him good. I played quite a few jobs for him. Now let me explain what I mean by for him. I'm playing with my own band, see, and he's got two jobs, and he's got to get rid of one in some kind of way, because he can't play with one. So several times I went on jobs that he had to fill his place up. I even went to one place and one night people didn't want to pay us because we wasn't Chris and he was like, you can't bear with the people.
What do you, how did you rate his hand? Oh, I thought he, I thought he'd done good. Was he a reader?

No, I don't know about that. That's one thing I wouldn't say, yeah, no. You never saw him read? Never seen him read, no. No, no. But, uh, it usually was this. All these fellas who could do good without music, they didn't read. They thought it was too hard of a job. I see. So they wouldn't.
You saw his band play several times?
Yeah. Oh yeah, plenty of times. He never used the violin, did he? No, no, no, no. Never used the violin, no. You think violin was only used in the bands that read?
